Is your company moving forward with AI, or just trying it out?

What it is for

Six questions your board will end up asking

Almost every company has AI pilots. Very few can answer these without opening six spreadsheets. SEVEN-G is built to answer them.

01Am I moving forward with AI?How many initiatives come in, how many reach production, where they get stuck and how long they take. A funnel, as in sales. 02Are my use cases profitable?Full cost against efficiencies and return. Only validated value adds up: "freed" capacity that nobody turns into savings does not count. 03Could my company do more?Nine impact spheres and three ambition levels show where value is still unexplored, and maturity tells you whether you are ready. 04Am I transforming, or just getting more efficient?An index with eight signals tells evidenced transformation apart from the kind that only exists on a slide. 05Do I know when to stop?Eight phases with decision gates. Stopping an initiative with a recorded reason and lesson is an outcome, not a failure. 06Is risk under control?Inventory, risk matrix, segregated roles —whoever builds does not audit— and orderly evidence for whatever regulation applies to you.

Is it profitable?

What the board needs to see, on one screen

The same register feeds a dashboard for the board of directors: costs, return, annual net and how much of that value has been validated by management control.

Swipe the image to see all of it.

  • Annual net of the portfolioCosts, efficiencies and return, with and without cross-cutting platforms.
    ?

    What it shows. Investment, recurring costs, efficiencies and return for each case and the annual net that remains; what is already being obtained versus what could be, and where additional investment would pay off most. Also agility: days from idea to approval and from approval to production, by risk level.

    What the board can decide. Reinforce what contributes most, rethink or retire negative nets with no strategic reason and steer the budget towards the units with the highest return; unblock stalled cases and see whether the bottleneck is approving (governance) or delivering (capacity).

  • Traffic lights nobody can dress upValidated value, regulatory classification and complete controls.
    ?

    How far to trust the figures. How much of the value is validated by management control and how much released capacity has not yet become real savings. The board does not accept unvalidated benefits and asks for a plan to realise that capacity.

    What risk is being taken. Each case's classification under the AI Act (the company's view versus the advisory board's), incidents and breaches with their response times and notifications, controls over agents and assistants, and exposure to AI-enabled attacks. The board requires pending classifications, puts conditions on high-risk cases and sets its risk appetite.

    Whether the information is enough. The data-quality light flags what the company does not yet report, so it can be requested with a deadline.

  • On your phone tooA pocket version to take into the board session.
    ?

    Six views. Portfolio and value, Funnel and life cycle, History and adoption, Risk and compliance, Inventory and Glossary; everything can be filtered by company, unit, status or type of case, and each block shows the conclusion first and the detail on a click.

    From one session to the next. A snapshot of the dashboard is saved at the close of each session: it compares how value, costs and cases evolve and measures whether what was launched is really used. The board reinforces training where use is low, retires what is not used and checks that commitments move forward.

The portfolio, case by case

?

How to read it. Every case, ungrouped. In use: actual annual cost and net and the share of its value validated by management control; in progress: the forecast ("fcst."), which does not add to the net; "no data" is never zero. In the dashboard, the inventory is grouped by company and unit with totals, and each case has a card: what it is, what it is for, its status and its figures.

What the board can decide. Spot duplicates that could be merged, check the balance between cost savings, growth and service, and choose which cases are rolled out across the organisation.

In short. The board moves from receiving reports to asking questions with data: how much does it contribute?, how much is validated?, what has stalled and why?, what risk are we taking?, what has changed since the last session? What it decides is kept in the recommendations register, to follow it up.

Do I know when to stop? Is risk under control?

A gate before every big spend

Every initiative goes through eight phases, from idea to operation. Between phases there is a gate with five possible outcomes: continue, continue with conditions, iterate, pivot or stop.

The third one is the one that matters: feasibility and risk, before the heavy investment. And no gate is passed on results alone: it takes the objective met and the evidence that proves it.

See how an initiative flows →

Could you do more? Are you transforming?

From one-off savings to transformation you can prove

A map of nine spheres by three ambition levels —optimise, augment, transform— shows where your AI is today and where you have not looked yet.

A maturity assessment across seven dimensions tells you which step the organisation is on, from 0 —chaos or scattered proofs of concept— to 5 —optimised, with evidenced transformation—, and the transformation index separates what is proven from what is merely declared.

See it for yourself

QUICK-CHECK: verify the framework with real example data

No need to read anything first. Open or download what SEVEN-G actually generates from the example initiative register, with what you are looking at in each case and where in the methodology it comes from.

The portfolio funnel

What you are looking at: the fictitious initiatives of the register across their stages —proposed, value hypothesis, proof of concept, in development—, with what fell away at each one and what has already reached use.

How you get there: each initiative is registered and moves phase by phase through the lifecycle's decision gates (document 20); the funnel only counts what is still in flight.

Open the funnel →

The board dashboard

What you are looking at: that same register turned into what the board sees —cost, return and net of the portfolio— and how much of that value is validated rather than merely estimated.

How you get there: the register becomes a dashboard with no retyping — the tool that generates it reads the register's JSON every time it changes.

Full dashboard →Mobile dashboard →

The risk matrix, as an Excel file

What you are looking at: the 5×5 probability-by-impact matrix of the fictitious initiatives; from there, any single case downloads an Excel file with its risk register and the mitigation and contingency plans the methodology proposes.

How you get there: risk is registered from phase 3 onward (document 33, template P12); the Excel file is generated by the tool in your own browser, with nothing uploaded to any server.

Open the risk matrix →

The transformation index

What you are looking at: whether the example portfolio is truly transforming or just getting more efficient, with the eight signals behind that answer —or the lack of them— and what would move it.

How you get there: the signals are defined in document 12; the tool calculates them on its own from the register whenever the data exists, and leaves what is missing as "no data" — it never estimates it.
